polities.name: Minoan Civilization
polities.note: Europe's first palace civilisation, a Bronze Age sea power based on Crete

polities.name: Mycenaean Greece
polities.note: warrior kingdoms of Bronze Age Greece whose collapse opened the Greek Dark Age

polities.name: Urnfield Culture
polities.note: Central European cremation-burial culture, ancestral to the Iron Age Celts

polities.name: Celtic Peoples
polities.note: Hallstatt and La Tene peoples spread from Iberia to Anatolia until Rome absorbed them

polities.name: Greek City-States
polities.note: hundreds of poleis led by Athens and Sparta; source of democracy, philosophy and drama

polities.name: Macedon
polities.note: Philip II's kingdom, then Alexander's conquest of Persia, which carried Greek rule to the Indus

polities.name: Roman Republic
polities.note: a city-state with a mixed constitution that conquered Italy and then the Mediterranean

polities.name: Roman Empire
polities.note: the whole Mediterranean world under one state, and the model every later European empire claimed

polities.name: Western Roman Empire
polities.note: the Latin half, dismembered by Goths, Vandals and Franks until the last emperor was deposed

polities.name: Byzantine Empire
polities.note: the Greek-speaking Roman Empire, which outlived the west by a thousand years

polities.name: Visigothic Kingdom
polities.note: Germanic successor state in Gaul and Iberia; later Spanish kingdoms claimed its inheritance

polities.name: Frankish Empire
polities.note: Charlemagne's empire, split at Verdun into the seeds of France and Germany

polities.name: Holy Roman Empire
polities.note: a confederation of German and Italian princes holding the revived Roman imperial title

polities.name: Papal States
polities.note: the pope's temporal realm in central Italy and the seat of Latin Christendom

polities.name: Republic of Venice
polities.note: a merchant republic that grew out of Byzantine Italy to dominate Mediterranean trade

polities.name: Norse and Vikings
polities.note: Scandinavian raiders, traders and settlers who reached Kiev, Normandy and Newfoundland

polities.name: Kievan Rus
polities.note: the first East Slavic state, which took Orthodox Christianity from Byzantium

polities.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
polities.note: wealthy imperial kingdom whose capital Prague led the Empire and birthed the Hussite revolt

polities.name: England
polities.note: Anglo-Saxon kingdom remade by Danish and Norman conquest, united with Scotland in 1707

polities.name: British Empire
polities.note: the largest empire in history, ruling a quarter of the world's land at its height

1815: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
1880: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
1914: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
1938: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

polities.name: Kingdom of France
polities.note: the Capetian realm that grew from Paris into Europe's most powerful monarchy under Louis XIV

polities.name: French Empire
polities.note: revolutionary and Napoleonic France, then the second-largest colonial empire until decolonisation

polities.name: Spanish Empire
polities.note: the first global empire, funded by American silver, on which the sun never set

polities.name: Portuguese Empire
polities.note: born of the Reconquista, it opened the sea route to India and held Brazil, Africa and Macau

polities.name: Dutch Republic and Empire
polities.note: a merchant republic that broke from Spain and ran the world's first great trading company

polities.name: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
polities.note: an elective monarchy and the largest state in 17th-century Europe, erased by three partitions

polities.name: Swedish Empire
polities.note: Gustavus Adolphus's Sweden ruled the Baltic and decided the Thirty Years' War

polities.name: Habsburg Monarchy
polities.note: the Habsburgs' composite realm of Austria, Bohemia and Hungary, Christendom's shield against the Ottomans

polities.name: Austria-Hungary
polities.note: the Dual Monarchy of eleven nationalities, whose collapse in 1918 remade central Europe

polities.name: Prussia
polities.note: a militarised Hohenzollern state that outfought Austria and unified Germany under Bismarck

polities.name: German Empire
polities.note: Bismarck's unified Germany, Europe's leading industrial and military power before 1914

polities.name: Nazi Germany
polities.note: the Third Reich, which overran most of Europe, murdered millions and was destroyed in total war

polities.name: Germany
polities.note: divided in 1949, reunified in 1990, and the economic anchor of the European Union

polities.name: Muscovy
polities.note: Moscow's princes shed Mongol overlordship and gathered the Rus lands into a tsardom

polities.name: Russian Empire
polities.note: stretched from Poland to the Pacific and broke Napoleon, but fell apart in war and revolution

polities.name: Soviet Union
polities.note: the first communist state and a nuclear superpower that split the postwar world in two

polities.name: Russian Federation
polities.note: the largest Soviet successor state, still spanning eleven time zones

polities.name: Italy
polities.note: unified in 1861 from a peninsula of kingdoms; a fascist empire, then a founding EU member

polities.name: European Union
polities.note: Europe's first union built by treaty rather than conquest, and the world's largest single market

polities.name: Sumer
polities.note: the world's first cities, writing and law, in the marshes of southern Mesopotamia

polities.name: Ancient Egypt
polities.note: three thousand years of pharaonic rule on the Nile, from the pyramids to Cleopatra

polities.name: Akkadian Empire
polities.note: Sargon's conquest of the Sumerian cities produced the first empire in history

polities.name: Babylonia
polities.note: Hammurabi's law code and, a millennium later, Nebuchadnezzar's Neo-Babylonian revival

polities.name: Hittite Empire
polities.note: Anatolian iron-age rival that fought Egypt to a draw at Kadesh before the Bronze Age collapse

polities.name: Assyria
polities.note: the first true military superpower, holding Mesopotamia to Egypt before a sudden total collapse

polities.name: Phoenicia and Carthage
polities.note: Levantine traders who spread the alphabet and founded Carthage, Rome's great western rival

polities.name: Achaemenid Persia
polities.note: the largest empire the world had yet seen, ruling perhaps two in five living people

polities.name: Seleucid Empire
polities.note: the largest fragment of Alexander's empire, spreading Greek cities from Syria to the Indus

polities.name: Parthian Empire
polities.note: horse-archer empire that held Rome at the Euphrates for nearly three centuries

polities.name: Kingdom of Kush
polities.note: Nubian kingdom of Napata and Meroe whose kings ruled Egypt as its 25th Dynasty

polities.name: Nok Culture
polities.note: West Africa's earliest known ironworking and terracotta sculpture tradition

polities.name: Kingdom of Aksum
polities.note: Red Sea trading power that minted its own coinage and adopted Christianity in the 4th century

polities.name: Sassanid Persia
polities.note: the last pre-Islamic Persian empire, Byzantium's equal until both were exhausted by war

polities.name: Rashidun Caliphate
polities.note: in thirty years the first caliphs took Persia, Egypt and the Levant

polities.name: Umayyad Caliphate
polities.note: stretched from Spain to the Indus, the largest empire on Earth in its day

polities.name: Abbasid Caliphate
polities.note: Baghdad's golden age of science and translation, ended by the Mongol sack of 1258

polities.name: Ghana Empire
polities.note: first of the Sahelian gold empires, controlling the trans-Saharan trade in gold and salt

polities.name: Fatimid Caliphate
polities.note: Shia rival caliphate that founded Cairo and ruled from Tunisia to Syria

polities.name: Seljuk Empire
polities.note: Turkic dynasty that took Baghdad, broke Byzantine Anatolia and provoked the Crusades

polities.name: Great Zimbabwe
polities.note: dry-stone capital of a Shona gold-trading state linked to the Indian Ocean coast

polities.name: Ayyubid Sultanate
polities.note: Saladin's dynasty, which reunited Egypt with Syria and retook Jerusalem in 1187

polities.name: Mali Empire
polities.note: Mansa Musa's gold empire, with Timbuktu as a centre of Islamic scholarship

polities.name: Mamluk Sultanate
polities.note: slave-soldier regime in Cairo that stopped the Mongols and ended the Crusader states

polities.name: Ottoman Empire
polities.note: took Constantinople in 1453 and ruled the Balkans, Anatolia and the Arab world for six centuries

polities.name: Kingdom of Kongo
polities.note: Central African state that converted to Christianity and traded, then unravelled, with Portugal

polities.name: Songhai Empire
polities.note: largest of the Sahelian empires, destroyed by a Moroccan army with gunpowder at Tondibi

polities.name: Safavid Persia
polities.note: made Shia Islam the state faith of Iran and rebuilt Isfahan as a world capital

polities.name: Ethiopian Empire
polities.note: Solomonic Christian monarchy, the one African state to defeat a European empire and stay free

polities.name: Iran
polities.note: Qajar and Pahlavi Iran and the Islamic Republic that replaced them in 1979

polities.name: Zulu Kingdom
polities.note: Shaka's military revolution reshaped southern Africa and checked the British at Isandlwana

polities.name: Colonial Africa
polities.note: composite ribbon for the European partition of Africa, from the Berlin Conference to independence

polities.name: South Africa
polities.note: the continent's industrial heartland, through apartheid and its negotiated end in 1994

polities.name: Turkey
polities.note: Ataturk's secular republic built on the Anatolian core of the fallen Ottoman state

polities.name: Saudi Arabia
polities.note: guardian of Mecca and Medina, transformed by oil into a decisive economic power

polities.name: Israel
polities.note: founded in former Ottoman and British Mandate territory, at the centre of the modern Middle East

polities.name: Indus Valley Civilisation
polities.note: largest Bronze Age civilisation by area, with planned brick cities and an undeciphered script

polities.name: Shang Dynasty
polities.note: first Chinese state confirmed by writing, via oracle-bone divination records

polities.name: Zhou Dynasty
polities.note: longest Chinese dynasty; its slow collapse into warring states produced Confucius, Laozi and Chinese political philosophy

polities.name: Maurya Empire
polities.note: first empire to unify almost all of South Asia; Ashoka's edicts spread Buddhism across Asia

polities.name: Qin Dynasty
polities.note: unified China in a single generation and set the imperial template that lasted 2,100 years

polities.name: Xiongnu Confederation
polities.note: first steppe empire; forced the Han into tribute and set the nomad-versus-farmer pattern of Eurasian history

polities.name: Han Dynasty
polities.note: Rome's eastern equal; opened the Silk Road and gave the Chinese majority its name

polities.name: Three Kingdoms
polities.note: Wei, Shu and Wu split the Han inheritance, becoming East Asia's most retold historical drama

polities.name: Jin Dynasty
polities.note: briefly reunified China in 280, then lost the north and preserved classical culture in the south

polities.name: Yamato Japan
polities.note: first unified Japanese state; imported Chinese writing, Buddhism and law codes

polities.name: Gupta Empire
polities.note: classical golden age of India; gave the world the decimal place-value system and the zero

polities.name: Gokturk Khaganate
polities.note: first empire to call itself Turk, stretching from Manchuria to the Black Sea and linking Byzantium to China

polities.name: Sui Dynasty
polities.note: reunified China after three centuries of division and dug the Grand Canal that still binds north to south

polities.name: Tang Dynasty
polities.note: the cosmopolitan peak of the Chinese world order; Chang'an was the largest city on Earth

polities.name: Srivijaya
polities.note: maritime hegemon of the Malacca and Sunda straits and a great centre of Buddhist learning

polities.name: Heian Japan
polities.note: aristocratic court culture that produced the world's first novel and a distinctly Japanese identity

polities.name: Khmer Empire
polities.note: mainland Southeast Asia's dominant power; Angkor was the largest pre-industrial city ever built

polities.name: Goryeo
polities.note: gave Korea its name and printed with movable metal type two centuries before Gutenberg

polities.name: Dai Viet (Vietnam)
polities.note: won independence from China in 939 and held it for nine centuries, expanding south to the Mekong

polities.name: Song Dynasty
polities.note: the world's richest and most technologically advanced economy: gunpowder, printing, paper money, the compass

polities.name: Kamakura Shogunate
polities.note: first warrior government of Japan; repelled two Mongol invasions

polities.name: Delhi Sultanate
polities.note: established lasting Muslim rule in India and shielded the subcontinent from Mongol conquest

polities.name: Mongol Empire
polities.note: largest contiguous land empire in history, briefly making Eurasia a single connected space

polities.name: Yuan Dynasty
polities.note: first foreign dynasty to rule all China; Marco Polo's Cathay

polities.name: Majapahit
polities.note: Java-based maritime empire claimed today as the ancestor of the Indonesian archipelago state

polities.name: Ashikaga Shogunate
polities.note: weak centre that produced Zen aesthetics, Noh and tea ceremony before dissolving into civil war

polities.name: Ming Dynasty
polities.note: restored native rule, sent Zheng He's treasure fleets to Africa, then turned inward

polities.name: Timurid Empire
polities.note: Timur's brutal Central Asian empire, whose Samarkand and Herat courts led the Islamic world in science and art

polities.name: Joseon
polities.note: five centuries of Confucian Korean rule; created the hangul alphabet, ended by Japanese annexation

polities.name: Mughal Empire
polities.note: at its height held a quarter of world GDP and built the Taj Mahal; hollowed out by the East India Company

polities.name: Tokugawa Shogunate
polities.note: two and a half centuries of enforced peace and near-total isolation, ended by American gunboats

polities.name: Qing Dynasty
polities.note: Manchu conquerors who doubled China's territory and ruled a third of humanity before collapsing under Western pressure

polities.name: British Raj
polities.note: the jewel of the British Empire, whose partition created the two states of modern South Asia

polities.name: Empire of Japan
polities.note: first non-Western industrial great power; its imperial expansion ended in total defeat in 1945

polities.name: Republic of China
polities.note: ended 2,100 years of imperial rule; after 1949 survives on Taiwan

polities.name: Japan
polities.note: post-war pacifist constitution and an economic miracle that made it the world's second-largest economy

polities.name: Republic of India
polities.note: the world's most populous country and largest democracy

polities.name: Pakistan
polities.note: created as a Muslim homeland at partition; lost its eastern wing as Bangladesh in 1971

polities.name: People's Republic of China
polities.note: lifted hundreds of millions out of poverty to become the second superpower of the 21st century

polities.name: Clovis and Paleo-Indian Peoples
polities.note: first continent-wide culture of the Americas; every later American society descends from this founding population

polities.name: Olmec Civilization
polities.note: Mesoamerica's mother culture: colossal heads, the ballgame, and the calendar and glyph traditions everyone after inherited

polities.name: Zapotec Civilization (Monte Alban)
polities.note: Oaxaca's mountaintop capital, home to the earliest true writing and calendar system in the Americas

polities.name: Teotihuacan
polities.note: largest city in the pre-Columbian Americas at roughly 125,000 people, its politics and art reaching into the Maya lowlands

polities.name: Maya City-States
polities.note: never one empire but a competing constellation of kingdoms holding the only full writing system in the Americas

polities.name: Toltec Empire
polities.note: Tula's hegemony over central Mexico, claimed as ancestral by every later Mesoamerican dynasty including the Aztecs

polities.name: Aztec Empire
polities.note: Triple Alliance tribute empire of some six million; Tenochtitlan was among the largest cities on Earth when Cortes arrived

polities.name: Chavin Culture
polities.note: the Andes' first pan-regional religious horizon, setting the template every later Andean state built on

polities.name: Moche Civilization
polities.note: north-coast Peruvian lords of adobe pyramids, desert irrigation, and the finest portrait ceramics in the Americas

polities.name: Tiwanaku
polities.note: Lake Titicaca ceremonial capital whose colonies and iconography spread across the southern Andes

polities.name: Wari Empire
polities.note: first true Andean empire: administrative centres, terracing and the highland road network the Inca later inherited

polities.name: Inca Empire
polities.note: Tawantinsuyu, the largest empire of the pre-Columbian world: two million square kilometres bound by roads and khipu

polities.name: Ancestral Puebloans
polities.note: Chaco Canyon's great houses and the Mesa Verde cliff dwellings, abandoned in the thirteenth-century megadrought

polities.name: Mississippian Culture
polities.note: maize-fed mound-building chiefdoms; Cahokia was the largest city north of Mexico until Philadelphia passed it in the 1780s

polities.name: Iroquois Confederacy
polities.note: Haudenosaunee league of five then six nations that held the balance between New France and British America for a century

polities.name: Powhatan Confederacy
polities.note: paramount chiefdom of thirty-odd Algonquian tribes that Jamestown landed inside, and that England broke within forty years

polities.name: Comancheria
polities.note: horse-borne southern-plains power that checked Spanish, Mexican and Texan expansion for a century and a half

polities.name: Viceroyalty of New Spain
polities.note: the silver viceroyalty that bankrolled Habsburg Spain, running from Oregon to Costa Rica and across the Pacific to Manila

polities.name: Viceroyalty of Peru
polities.note: Potosi's silver mountain made this the richest colony on Earth; its dismemberment produced most of South America

polities.name: Portuguese Brazil
polities.note: sugar, then gold, then coffee, and the only European colony ever to host its own mother country's exiled court

polities.name: New France
polities.note: a fur-trade empire claiming the St Lawrence, Great Lakes and Mississippi with barely seventy thousand settlers

polities.name: British America
polities.note: thirteen Atlantic colonies plus the northern conquests, 2.5 million people and a tax revolt by 1776

polities.name: United States
polities.note: thirteen colonies to continental then global hegemon; the dominant power on Earth from 1945

polities.name: Canada
polities.note: Confederation fused British and French North America into a transcontinental dominion, fully sovereign by stages to 1982

polities.name: Mexico
polities.note: inherited New Spain's vast north, lost half of it by 1848, then remade itself in a decade of revolution

polities.name: Brazil
polities.note: the one Latin American state to win independence as a monarchy, and the only one to keep a whole colonial empire intact

polities.name: Gran Colombia
polities.note: Bolivar's union of modern Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama, which fell apart into its parts within twelve years

polities.name: Argentina
polities.note: grain and beef made it one of the ten richest countries on Earth by 1913, followed by a century of relative decline

polities.name: Aboriginal Australian Nations
polities.note: hundreds of nations and 250-odd languages across a continent, the longest continuous cultural tradition on Earth

polities.name: Lapita and Polynesian Expansion
polities.note: the greatest maritime colonisation in history: Lapita potters out of the Bismarcks to every habitable Pacific island

polities.name: Hawaiian Kingdom
polities.note: Kamehameha's unification produced an internationally recognised Pacific monarchy, overthrown by American planters in 1893

polities.name: Maori Iwi of Aotearoa
polities.note: the last major landmass on Earth settled by humans; the iwi ceded governance under the Treaty of Waitangi in 1840

polities.name: Australia
polities.note: penal colony to gold-rush settler society to federated Commonwealth in 1901, on a continent taken without treaty
